opcode.name: OP_WearChange
opcode.comment: Spawn-state / appearance broadcast (multi-slot). Header=wearChangeStruct(11B), then slotCount*wearChangeSlotStruct(16B+varname), then 2B pad. count=0→13B (hash refresh), count=N→header+N slots (~+23B/slot incl short name). slotCount@9 correlates with size; unk8=1 in equipment samples. Re-confirmed equipment form 2026-05-27 (wearchange-clean: 30 fires on equip/remove, 13B refresh, field@4=material code). POLYMORPHIC: this same wire opcode also carries buff-icon arrays (21B blocks: {spellID, value, caster-name\0}) as a spawn-state broadcast — multiple spawn ids, fires on zone-in and around buff events. Those variants don't match SpawnUpdateStruct (SZC_Match) so they're unhandled, but appear in --list-events/--dump-payload — do NOT mistake them for a buff/BuffQuery opcode (cost a full 2026-05-27 hunt). Dedicated buff broadcast is OP_Buff 0x18b4 (trailing flag distinguishes).

opcode.name: OP_BuffQuery
opcode.comment: [STALE post-07/15 patch — was 0x306c; re-hunt on current patch] C>S: {u32 buff_slot, u32 self_spawn_id} (8 bytes). Client requests server reconfirm buff slot N at zone-in. Fires once per occupied buff slot on the SECOND zone-in after a buff was applied (not the first — the buff must survive one full zone cycle before the client requests verification). Server responds with OP_Buff for that slot. Wire-verified: slot=0 → OP_Buff IVU(225) spellslot=0; slot=1 → DE(352) spellslot=1; slot=2/1/0 → SLW/SoW/Regen.

opcode.name: OP_BuffWindow
opcode.comment: S>C: fires 10x per zone-in (slots 0-9), one packet per slot. Payload: {u32 slot, u32 spellid=0xffffffff_empty, u32 pad} (12 bytes). Initializes the short-duration buff window at zone-in. Field2 always 0xffffffff in all observed captures — long-duration buffs come via OP_Buff / the buff-bar sync instead. Never fires mid-session. Re-confirmed 2026-05-27 (buffquery-fresh2: 30 fires = 10 slots × 3 zone-ins, byte-exact). The prior 0x3f37 assignment (2026-05-25) was a misidentification — 0x3f37 does not fire at all in clean buff captures.

opcode.name: OP_SpawnAppearance2
opcode.comment: [STALE post-07/15 patch — was 0x8cd3; re-hunt on current patch] Extended 24-byte bidirectional appearance update — spawnAppearance2Struct {u32 spawn_id, u32 type, u32 value, u8[12] pad}. C>S type=0x24 (36) with spawn_id=0 = OP_ClickBuffOff (buff_slot in value field); acknowledged, unwired. S>C fires carry guild/cast/appearance types and co-occur with buff landing messages. Distinct from OP_SpawnAppearance. Re-confirmed post-2026-05-22 patch: type set {5,6,8,22,26,36,42} matches; ClickBuffOff C>S type=0x24 fires with spawn_id=0, varying buff_slot. type=0x2c (44) S>C = TLP-ruleset mob-lock / FTE attackable flag: value=0 = attackable (fires ~5-7s after a fresh spawn's OP_ZoneEntry — the grey→attackable transition), value=1 = locked/engaged (fires when a mob is claimed; observed firing for the engaged target exactly at engage time). Per-spawn 0/1 toggle, balanced across a session; absent on standard Live (mobs always attackable). Confirmed 2026-05-27 on a locked TLP server (moblock.vpk): fresh spawns 14245/14247/14264 each spawn→value=0 after ~5-7s; engaged target 13799 → value=1 at engage. Wired to Spawn.locked → web UI. 2026-07-13: payload flipped uint8_t/none → spawnAppearance2Struct/match so the wire_live typename binds exactly (the old entry only worked via the dispatch last-payload fallback, now removed).
